proposals.before: With Chen Chi he stormed Dongguan, took it, and received brevet provincial commander rank.
proposals.after: With Chen Shi he stormed Dongguan, took it, and received brevet provincial commander rank.
proposals.reason: 陳湜 is Chen Shi (Chén Shí); Chi misreads the character 湜.

proposals.before: He again joined Chen Chi in attacking Dongguan, took it, and was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
proposals.after: He again joined Chen Shi in attacking Dongguan, took it, and was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
proposals.reason: 陳湜 is Chen Shi; literal English wrongly romanizes as Chen Chi.

proposals.before: In the fourth month they jointly assaulted Jingzhuguan: Li Chaobin on the upper river, Yisheng on the lower. The rebels were pinned by the fleet and could not look inland.
proposals.after: In the fourth month they jointly assaulted Jinzhu Pass: Li Chaobin on the upper river, Yisheng on the lower. The rebels were pinned by the fleet and could not look inland.
proposals.reason: 金柱關 is conventionally Jinzhu Pass / Golden Pillar Pass; Jingzhuguan is an opaque transcription.

proposals.before: He garrisoned Huangshiji, struck Wuhu rebels, and fought at Pangji, Yinjahui, and Zongyang with distinction, earning promotion to coordinator.
proposals.after: He garrisoned Huangshiji, struck Wuhu rebels, and fought at Xianji, Yinjiahui, and Zongyang with distinction, earning promotion to coordinator.
proposals.reason: 蟂磯 is Xianji (or similar); Pangji is a misreading of 蟂磯; 殷家匯 is Yinjiahui not Yinjahui.

proposals.before: The forward mobile commander was posted to Hankou and the rear mobile commander to Liumen.
proposals.after: The forward mobile commander was posted to Hongkou and the rear mobile commander to Liumen.
proposals.reason: 谾口 is not Hankou (漢口); the translation invents the famous Hankou place-name.

proposals.before: Pressing Huzhou from Jiapu on Changxing, he faced tens of thousands of rebels fortifying the hills; while Yang Dingxun and Liu Shiji held the front, Chaobin landed his sailors on the rear in a pincer and destroyed every northwest river fort.
proposals.after: Pressing Huzhou from Jiapu toward Changxing, he faced tens of thousands of rebels fortifying the hills; while Yang Dingxun and Liu Shiji held the front, Chaobin landed his sailors on the rear in a pincer and destroyed every northwest river fort.
proposals.reason: 由夾浦逼長興 means advancing from Jiapu to press Changxing; "on Changxing" misreads the directional 逼.

proposals.before: At Tianjiazhen he led ten boats in a forty-li chase, destroyed rebel shipping, and was raised to coordinator.
proposals.after: At Tianjiazhen he led ten boats in a chase of more than forty li, destroyed rebel shipping, and was raised to coordinator.
proposals.reason: 四十餘裡 should be 四十餘里 (li); the translation omits "more than" for 餘.

decisions.reason: The name 陳湜 is Chen Shi; Chi does not match the reading Shí already preserved in the extraction's pinyin.
The paired literal field contains the same incorrect reading of 陳湜 and must use Chen Shi.
金柱關 is Jinzhu Pass; Jingzhuguan misreads 金 and redundantly retains guan after translating it as Pass.

decisions.after: He garrisoned Huangshiji, struck Wuhu rebels, and fought at Xiaoji, Yinjiahui, and Zongyang with distinction, earning promotion to coordinator.
decisions.reason: 蟂 is read xiao, so the place is Xiaoji, not Pangji or the proposal's Xianji; 殷家匯 is Yinjiahui.
The source has 谾口, not 漢口; Hongkou follows the reading of 谾 and avoids inventing Hankou.
由夾浦逼長興 means advancing from Jiapu to press Changxing; 'on Changxing' is not idiomatic or syntactically accurate.
四十餘里 means more than forty li, so the idiomatic field should retain 餘.

claimRevisions.reason: The structured name must match the corrected reading of 湜.
The event place should use the same corrected English form as the chapter text.
